Instruction TTS.primary_help: Words you want the model to speak. Do not put voice directions here.
Instruction TTS.secondary_help: Describe voice character, tone, accent, or delivery. This description is used in the TTS prompt.
Instruction TTS.requirement: No audio required. Enter the words to speak and a voice description.
Instruction TTS.example: Target text: Welcome back. | Voice description: A warm, clear young female voice.
Instruction TTS.note: Use a short test sentence and a concise voice description. Automatic duration follows the target text. Base exposes sampling controls; Flash always uses 4 steps and CFG 0.

Voice cloning.primary_help: New words to speak in the reference speaker's voice.
Voice cloning.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; a reference transcript or extra voice directions are not added to the cloning prompt.
Voice cloning.requirement: Connect clear reference speech from one speaker. Enter only the new words to speak.
Voice cloning.example: Target text: Hello, and welcome to today's program.
Voice cloning.note: Use clean, single-speaker reference speech. The reference supplies the voice; the first box supplies new words. Try different seeds for pronunciation variation, then fix the chosen seed.

Speech text editing.primary_label: Edit request (one change at a time)
Speech text editing.secondary_label: Full source transcript (optional, duration estimate only)
Speech text editing.primary_help: One exact edit, such as Replace 'Los Angeles' with 'Florida'. Also supports Insert 'everyone' after 'Hello' and Delete 'um'.
Speech text editing.secondary_help: Optional full transcript of the CROPPED SOURCE audio, before the edit. Used only to estimate output duration; it is not a prompt or transcript correction.
Speech text editing.requirement: Connect ordinary spoken audio. Make one replacement, insertion, or deletion, using the exact original words.
Speech text editing.note: Prefer Base. Crop to the sentence around the edit with a little context. Match the original words exactly; use a longer unique phrase if they repeat. Set seed control to fixed for comparisons. Start with NFE 32, CFG 2, Sway -1; try a few seeds first, then compare NFE 48/64 or modest CFG changes one at a time. Extra instructions in box 2 are ignored. Check Final instruction and Run metadata.

Lyric editing.primary_label: Lyric replacement (one change at a time)
Lyric editing.secondary_label: Full source lyrics (optional, duration estimate only)
Lyric editing.primary_help: One lyric replacement using the exact sung words: Change 'hello tomorrow' to 'hello future' in the vocal recording.
Lyric editing.secondary_help: Optional full lyrics of the CROPPED SOURCE vocals, before the edit. Duration estimation only; not extra editing directions.
Lyric editing.requirement: Connect clean, isolated solo singing without accompaniment (a cappella). Replace one phrase matching the actual lyrics.
Lyric editing.example: Change 'hello tomorrow' to 'hello future' in the vocal recording.
Lyric editing.note: Use isolated, unaccompanied solo vocals and a short phrase with context. Do not use ordinary speech or a mix with accompaniment. Try Base and a fixed seed while comparing settings. Box 2 cannot steer pronunciation.

Pitch editing.primary_help: A signed semitone change: +1, +2, +3, -1, -2, or -3. Use the numeric form.
Pitch editing.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; additional prose here does not affect pitch.
Pitch editing.requirement: Connect audio. Supported changes are +/-1, +/-2, or +/-3 semitones.
Pitch editing.note: Duration follows the effective source speech. Use one supported step; zero is rejected. Preserve the same source and seed when comparing pitch choices.

Speed editing.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; additional prose here does not affect speed.
Speed editing.note: Below 1 slows speech; above 1 speeds it up. Duration is speech duration divided by the multiplier. Manual duration is ignored; trim the source if slowing it would exceed 30 seconds.

Volume editing.primary_help: A signed volume change: +5, +10, +15, -5, -10, or -15 dB.
Volume editing.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; additional prose here does not affect volume.
Volume editing.requirement: Connect audio. Supported changes are +/-5, +/-10, or +/-15 dB.
Volume editing.note: Positive values increase volume; negative values reduce it. Output protection may reduce peaks to prevent clipping, so requested amplification is not an unlimited gain control.

Emotion editing.primary_help: One target emotion: happy, angry, sad, fearful, surprised, disgusted, calm, or excited.
Emotion editing.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; additional emotional directions here are ignored.
Emotion editing.requirement: Connect spoken audio. Choose happy, angry, sad, fearful, surprised, disgusted, calm, or excited.
Emotion editing.note: Use spoken speech, not singing. Match request language to source speech where possible. Base is the recommended starting point. Emotion changes use automatic duration factors; manual duration does not override them.

Timbre editing.primary_help: A concise target voice description, such as A deep, resonant young male voice.
Timbre editing.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; put the voice description in box 1.
Timbre editing.requirement: Connect spoken audio and describe the desired voice.
Timbre editing.example: A deep, resonant young male voice
Timbre editing.note: Keeps the words while changing voice character. To speak new text, use TTS or Voice cloning instead. Try Base and several seeds; this is voice transformation, not an exact cloning control.

Accent removal.primary_help: A nonempty accent-removal request, such as Remove the regional accent. The action uses a fixed official prompt.
Accent removal.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; neither box selects a target accent or language.
Accent removal.requirement: Connect spoken audio with a regional or dialect accent.
Accent removal.note: Use speech with a regional/dialect accent. The task preserves speaker identity and content; custom accent instructions are not forwarded. Already-standard speech is not a useful comparison.

Nonverbal sound editing.primary_help: Specify one event and its location: Add laughter after 'welcome back', Add a sigh at the beginning, or Remove all breathing.
Nonverbal sound editing.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; the complete event request belongs in box 1.
Nonverbal sound editing.requirement: Connect audio. Add or remove one event, such as laughter, breathing, a sigh, or a cough.
Nonverbal sound editing.note: Use a quoted, exact spoken anchor for before/after placement. Unsupported events or missing positions are rejected. Duration changes automatically by event family; try seeds to compare event delivery.

Whisper conversion.primary_help: Convert to whisper or Convert to normal speech.
Whisper conversion.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; extra delivery directions here are ignored.
Whisper conversion.requirement: Connect spoken audio. Specify whisper conversion or a return to normal speech.
Whisper conversion.note: Use spoken audio, not singing. Whisper-to-normal preprocessing differs from normal-to-whisper. Base is the starting point; quiet whisper output is intentional.

Speech enhancement.primary_help: Specify cleanup: Remove noise, Remove room reverb, or Remove noise and room reverb.
Speech enhancement.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; cleanup choices belong in box 1.
Speech enhancement.requirement: Connect spoken audio to remove background noise and/or room reverberation.
Speech enhancement.note: Keeps all speakers and the source length. To isolate a speaker, use a separation task. Try a single cleanup type before requesting both; more CFG is not guaranteed to improve cleanup.

Audio quality repair.primary_help: Name the defect or repair: Restore high frequencies and clarity, Remove the telephone effect, megaphone, underwater, clipping, dropout, or DC offset.
Audio quality repair.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; put the repair request in box 1.
Audio quality repair.requirement: Connect spoken audio to restore high frequencies/bandwidth or repair telephone, megaphone, or underwater coloration.
Audio quality repair.example: Restore high frequencies and clarity; or: Remove the telephone effect
Audio quality repair.note: Use Speech enhancement for ordinary noise/reverb. Cleanup can be included in the primary request, e.g. Restore high frequencies and denoise. Repair regenerates audio and cannot guarantee recovery of missing detail.

Speaker separation.primary_help: Select by order of first speech: The first speaker, The second speaker, or Speaker 2.
Speaker separation.secondary_help: Optional supported cleanup keywords: denoise, dereverb, or both. Arbitrary style instructions are ignored.
Speaker separation.requirement: Connect audio with multiple speakers. Select a speaker by the order in which they start speaking.
Speaker separation.note: Use a clip containing the speaker's first appearance. Speaker order refers to the cropped clip, not the full recording. Output keeps the selected speaker and source length.

Music vocal extraction.primary_help: Keep only singing vocals or Keep all vocals (speech and singing).
Music vocal extraction.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; vocal selection belongs in box 1.
Music vocal extraction.requirement: Connect mixed audio with accompaniment and specify the vocals to retain.
Music vocal extraction.note: Use mixed audio with accompaniment. This task selects vocal categories; it does not select a named singer or generate a different melody. Source length is preserved.

Target speaker extraction.primary_help: A short, exact phrase already spoken by the target speaker in the source audio.
Target speaker extraction.secondary_help: Optional supported cleanup keywords: denoise, dereverb, or both. Arbitrary style instructions are ignored.
Target speaker extraction.requirement: Connect audio with multiple speakers. Enter a short, exact phrase spoken by the target speaker.
Target speaker extraction.note: The phrase identifies a speaker; it is not new text to generate. Use words unique to the target within the cropped clip. Output keeps that speaker and preserves source length.
